answer: Each identity lays one quartz fiber run and locks an 85-credit bond. The auditor sends a light pulse down the fiber and reads its echo map from the ivory ledger; echo peaks must match the published route map, and a missing peak, a reused fiber serial, or a peak shifted over 3 percent burns the bond. The first filing costs 38 credits, the kth 38+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6032; 1000 fakes pay 3,035,000 in fees and lock 85,000, each run needs its own crew. A rented-fiber ring fails: one fiber cannot show two distinct echo maps. An honest layer pays 38 once and reclaims the bond after audit.
